relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: Vidya Dehejia was educated at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, where she gained a first in ancient Indian culture in 1961.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: She gained a first in archaeology and anthropology at Newnham College, Cambridge in 1963.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: She completed her PhD on early Buddhist caves of Western India in 1968, also at Cambridge.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: In 1968, she took up a post-doctoral fellowship at the University of Sydney.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: In 1970 she became a lecturer at the University of Hong Kong.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.object: Delhi School of Planning and Architecture
relations.evidence: In 1973 she moved to a lectureship at the Delhi School of Planning and Architecture.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: In 1982 she became an associate professor at Columbia University.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.role: chief curator and deputy director of its Freer Gallery of Art and Arthur M. Sackler Gallery
relations.evidence: In 1994, she moved to the Smithsonian Institution, becoming the chief curator and deputy director of its Freer Gallery of Art and Arthur M. Sackler Gallery.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.role: Barbara Stoler Miller Professor of Indian Art
relations.evidence: In 2002 she became Barbara Stoler Miller Professor of Indian Art at Columbia University, and in 2003 she became the director of that university's South Asian Institute.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: She has been appointed to the Mario Miranda Visiting Research Professorship at Goa University.

relations.subject: Vidya Dehejia
relations.evidence: (With Pratapaditya Pal). From Merchants to Emperors: British Artists and India 1757–1930. Ithaca, New York: Cornell University Press, 1986.
